titel: Episode 587: Kier Gaines: Self-Awareness, Distress Tolerance, and the Mental Skills That Build Resilience

einzeiler: Kier Gaines on self-awareness, distress tolerance, and building mental resilience
kurzfassung: Kier Gaines discusses how personal growth requires confronting uncomfortable realities rather than relying on motivation or self-deception. The conversation explores the impact of technology, convenience, and modern loneliness on mental health and decision-making. Additionally, the episode addresses the overuse of clinical terminology online and the importance of actionable self-reflection.
stichpunkte: The difference between loving the fantasy of a goal and doing the work required to achieve it
How artificial intelligence compares to the emotional attunement and human connection of therapy
The impact of phones, algorithms, and disappearing third spaces on loneliness and connection
Why protecting your peace can sometimes function as well-dressed avoidance
How practicing small, low-stakes boundaries makes setting difficult boundaries easier
The societal pressures and overloaded systems that push people past their emotional limits
How overusing and misapplying mental health language online affects self-understanding
The effects of endless dating options and modern swipe culture on commitment and satisfaction
beschreibung:
What if the thing keeping you stuck is not a lack of motivation, but the stories you keep telling yourself about why you cannot move?
We spend a lot of time thinking about what we want to change, who we want to become, and what would finally make us feel better. But intentions alone do not create change. The way you talk to yourself, the discomfort you avoid, the boundaries you do not practice, the labels you attach to yourself and other people, and the actions you take when nobody is motivating you, all shape what happens next. Kier Gaines argues that real growth starts when you become willing to confront the parts of yourself you would rather explain away.
Self-awareness gives you something practical to work with. You can learn to tolerate discomfort instead of immediately escaping it, practice saying no before the stakes are high, question whether "protecting your peace" has become avoidance, and stop waiting for the perfect mood or moment to start. You can also become more intentional about how social media, constant convenience, comparison, and endless options are influencing the way you think, connect, and make decisions.
Kier Gaines is a licensed therapist, keynote speaker, and popular content creator who has inspired millions of people to become more proactive about their mental health. His work has been recognized by Oprah and Viola Davis, and he has been invited to speak at the White House, NASA, Amazon Movie Studios, and more. He is also a contributor to Men's Health, host of the podcast (L)Earned The Hard Way, and author of It All Starts When You Do, out September 1, 2026.
What's Discussed:
(08:25) Why people can fall in love with the fantasy of a goal while avoiding the work required to achieve it, and why action is what turns an idea into evidence.
(27:13) Where AI can be useful for journaling and reflection, and what gets lost when it replaces the silence, emotional attunement, and human connection of therapy.
(31:48) How phones, algorithms, convenience, and the disappearance of "third spaces" may be contributing to loneliness and weakening face-to-face connection.
(37:41) Why "protecting your peace" can become well-dressed avoidance, and how avoiding every uncomfortable interaction can lower your tolerance for normal stress.
(40:10) How practicing small, low-stakes "no's" can make it easier to set boundaries when the consequences feel bigger.
(45:55) Why feeling overwhelmed does not automatically mean you are incapable, and how lack of support, financial pressure, and overloaded systems can push people past their limit.
(52:44) Why mental health language is being overused online, from calling every difficult person a narcissist to oversimplifying anxious and avoidant attachment.
(57:46) How having more options can create more dissatisfaction, especially in dating, and why endless swiping can make it harder to commit to what is in front of you.
(1:05:14) Why affirmations without awareness and action are just words, and how toxic positivity can become another way to avoid what actually needs attention.
(1:14:08) How depression can show up as irritation, isolation, or loss of joy instead of obvious sadness, and why high-functioning people can miss the signs in themselves.
